Arrow Ludo Rules

Ludo with a shortcut: the board has arrows across the middle. Bring all four of your tokens around the track and into the finish before the others.

The rules

Like Ludo
Each player has 4 tokens. Roll the die and move one token by the number rolled. A token comes into play only on a 6, and a 6 gives another roll (three 6s in a row forfeit the turn). Landing on an opponent's token sends it back to its home base, except on the marked safe squares. Two tokens of one color on a square form a block that opponents can neither land on nor pass. A token needs an exact roll to reach the finish.
The arrow squares
Each color has one arrow square, the last square of its own arm, 12 steps after its start. The four arrow squares are marked with an arrow pointing at the middle, and two lines with arrowheads across the board join opposite pairs.
The flight
If your token lands exactly on your own arrow square, it flies across the middle at once and lands on the arrow square on the opposite side, 26 squares ahead. If an opponent's token stands there, it is sent home; if two opponent tokens form a block there, you cannot make that move. Passing the arrow square without stopping on it does nothing, and the arrow squares of other colors are ordinary squares for you.
Players
2 to 4 players on the classic board. You play one color, the others are computer opponents (Easy, Medium or Hard), or everyone plays on one device. The Hint button shows a good move for your roll. Each color has its own shape, so the game can be played without colors: red circle, green open circle, yellow triangle, blue open square.
